title: Meta Pixel, CAPI and deduplication
summary: Report real purchases without counting browser and server copies twice.
why: Valid purchase events support ad learning and evaluation.
Browser and server tracking complement each other, but duplicate purchases inflate ROAS.
know: Pixel sends browser events; CAPI sends server events. Neither is an SEO meta or Open Graph tag.
The core path includes ViewContent, AddToCart, InitiateCheckout and Purchase. Keep value, currency and product IDs consistent.
For the same event, match event_name and use the browser eventID as the server event_id. Reuse a stable ID for that action.
Shopify’s official Meta channel covers some events. Verify custom headless storefront coverage separately.
CAPI still requires appropriate consent. Sharing levels, customer data and purposes must follow approved rules.
inputs: Existing business/ad accounts, Pixel/dataset, catalog and access
Event ownership, product ID mappings, consent rules and test orders
actions: Inspect official channels, GTM, code and server senders. Assign clear event ownership.
Configure supported APIs/native integrations within authorization. Match content_ids to the catalog.
Use Test Events and diagnostics for purchases, rejected consent, reloads and retries. Inspect browser/server pairing.
Deliver de-identified payloads, timestamps, matched IDs and order-value reconciliation; list uncovered paths.
done: One test purchase becomes one valid conversion, with evidence of browser/server pairing.
Rejected sharing follows approved rules; events reveal no extra customer data.
pitfalls: Duplicating sends from the official app and manual Pixel.
Generating a new event_id on each retry or relying only on Pixel Helper.
decision: Agree on data sharing and channel use. Tracking setup and ad activation are separate decisions.

reader.concept: Meta tracking reports purchases to Facebook and Instagram advertising. Pixel sends from the browser; CAPI sends from the server.
reader.when: Use this before Meta campaigns or when purchase totals look wrong.

example.situation: Pixel and CAPI report one purchase without a shared identifier.
example.lesson: Match the reports to prevent counting it twice.

reader.first_step: Inventory Pixel, CAPI and official integrations; identify each sender.
terms: Browser code that records and sends events.
Conversions API for sending server events.
